citations.description: verify step has no model: key
Ticket scope: 'src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml — express the per-pass class as model: standard'

findings.criterion: a test asserts code-review's verify step resolves the `standard` class rather than `cfg.model`
findings.detail: The code-review.yaml `verify` step (lines 143-155) has no `model: standard` declaration — the ticket's scope explicitly required adding it. No test in the suite asserts that the code-review verify step resolves the standard class. Searches for 'code_review verify model', 'code-review verify step', and 'code_review verify standard' all returned no matches.

citations.description: Only plan-review path tested with non-default provider
verify step has no model: standard, so it uses cfg.model

findings.criterion: a test asserts that with classes configured for a non-default provider, no verifier path resolves a model belonging to a different provider
findings.detail: Only `test_the_verifier_follows_a_configured_standard_class` (test_verifier_class.py:49-66) tests this for the plan-review `_verifier_cfg` path. The completion verifier path and the code-review verify step are not tested with a non-default provider. Furthermore, since code-review.yaml's verify step has no `model: standard`, it would use `cfg.model` (the framework default) regardless of class config, meaning the code-review path would resolve a model from a different provider.

citations.description: resolve_verifier_model still exists with old equality logic
Old test still tests equality-based behavior, no enumeration test

findings.criterion: a test enumerates the consumers of `resolve_verifier_model` and asserts each resolves the standard class — `plan_review/__init__.py:_verifier_cfg` is one the plan had not enumerated
findings.detail: No such test exists. The `resolve_verifier_model` function still exists in review_kernel/verify.py with the OLD equality-based logic (line 269). While it is no longer called by verifier paths (only defined and exported), no test enumerates its consumers and asserts each resolves the standard class. The existing test `test_resolve_verifier_model_non_frontier_default` in test_review_kernel.py still tests the OLD equality-based behavior.

citations.description: xcheck test asserts drop behavior, not model resolution
xcheck.py:198 calls _verifier_cfg but no test asserts model resolution here

findings.criterion: a test asserts `_verifier_cfg` resolves the standard class, exercised through its real callers at `xcheck.py:198` and `xcheck.py:336` rather than in isolation
findings.detail: The xcheck tests (test_plan_review_xcheck.py) call `maybe_apply_contradiction` and `maybe_apply_comment_trail` which internally call `_verifier_cfg`, but no test asserts anything about the model that `_verifier_cfg` resolves through those callers. The tests only assert the drop behavior (which findings are dropped), not the model resolution.
